Each task asks the agent to make software behave exactly like a reference version that it can run but not read.
In the reimplementation tasks the agent writes a new program from scratch, in a language of its choice, from the reference and its documentation.
In the upgrade tasks the agent brings an existing repository up to the reference's newer release by changing its code.
In the migration tasks the agent ports a Java or Rust library to Go or C++ behind fixed signatures.
Hidden tests compare the result with the reference, output for output.
Gemini 4 Argon passes 39% of its runs on these tasks, and it fails every run on 27% of the tasks.
Gemini 3.8 Flash passes 1%, and it fails every run on 96% of the tasks.
The main languages are Agent's choice (42%), Go (23%) and C++ (13%).

| Domain | What the tasks do | % of catalog |
|---|---|---:|
| Languages & developer tooling | Rebuild or upgrade compilers, interpreters, API tools and command-line tools so they behave exactly like

Engineers often have to make software behave exactly like a version they cannot reuse: rebuilding a tool whose source is unavailable, bringing an old codebase up to a newer release, or replacing a Java or Rust dependency with a port in Go or C++.
In each case the specification is observable behaviour.
The hard part is inferring the rules from outputs and documentation, then matching exit codes, output, file effects, numeric precision and result ordering without seeing the tests.
Reimplementation and upgrade tasks give the agent a reference program it can run but not read.
For a reimplementation, the agent writes a source project and a `compile.sh` from the reference and its documentation.
For an upgrade, the agent changes an existing repository in `/app/repo`, which is built with a fixed `/opt/task/build.sh`.
Migration tasks provide the original source and a skeleton with final signatures, and most add a `mig-check` tool.
Every task runs offline, and hidden tests compare the result with the reference.
Reproduce the documented behaviour of an execute-only program, delivered as source code plus `compile.sh`.
Update an existing repository to match a reference program, after first writing a research and plan file.
Port a named Java or Rust library to Go or C++ from a reference folder, keeping the given signatures, within per-test time and memory limits.

children.text: A library engineer is replacing a Rust graph-layout dependency with a Go package.
The engineer has the crate source and a Go skeleton with final signatures.
The work is to read the layout stages in the Rust source and reproduce their output, including coordinates and edge points, in Go.
